target_customer: Workplaces, multifamily properties, fleets and site hosts that buy EV charging management software and services
problem: EV drivers without home charging struggle to find reliable charging, and site hosts lack tools for scheduling, access control and payments at shared chargers.
business_model: Software platform and services for charging site operators, with revenue share and fees from charging sessions and demand response programs
product_category: EV charging management software and network

founders.name: Thomas Sun
founders.background_notes: Only founder listed on the YC page. Company says it was started by EV drivers who lacked home charging.

founders.name: Timotej Gavrilovic
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder by InsideEVs, February 2020. Not on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed to integrate many charger hardware brands and protocols, payments and scheduling in software, with some hardware dependence.

defensibility.rationale: Charger management software had many vendors. Integrations with 20 plus hardware and service partners (Pulse 2, April 2020) and network growth gave limited lock in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbent networks stayed independent. AmpUp partnered with Enel X, Blink and others per InsideEVs (February 2020) and kept growing.

market_need_then: EV adoption was rising and workplace and multifamily charging was unreliable. InsideEVs (February 2020) described ampUp as community management software with scheduling, access control and payments for site hosts and drivers.

identity.voice_and_tone: Simple and reliable, such as making charging as simple as LED lights

brand_strength.rationale: Plain B2B tone and no independent press on the brand. Spelled ampUp and AmpUp in different sources.

pivots.from: Shared community charging app to build a network of charger owners
pivots.to: Software and services for workplaces, multifamily and fleets
pivots.why: Company site describes first releasing a mobile app for shared charging, then a platform for businesses. Exact date and reasons not stated.

outcome_analysis: AmpUp is active with about 45 people. It raised undisclosed strategic money from automakers in 2020, Goodyear in 2021, a 1.7 million dollar Connecticut grant in 2023 and a 15 million dollar Series A in September 2024, a long gap after YC. It added partnerships (Hubject, Tritium, Curo) in 2025. Growth was slower than a typical YC outcome and the amounts of early rounds are not public.
notes: Series A of 15 million dollars is stated by the company release and PR Newswire. Goodyear round and grant come from search summaries (Tyre Press and EV Engineering pages not opened). One profile lists total funding of 16.9 million dollars, an unverified aggregator figure. InsideEVs February 2020 names partners (Enel X, Blink, ClipperCreek, ControlMod) not competitors, and no source near the batch names rivals, so the competitor list is empty. Founder backgrounds were not found in opened sources. A late 2025 security incident involving its Stripe payment system was seen only in a law firm solicitation and is not recorded as fact.
